notes: Vegetative cells grown in LB to OD 0.4-0.5, then shifted to the treatment temperature; readout is in vivo thermal inactivation of a heterologous bacterial luciferase (bioluminescence decay), not cell killing. Rate constant Kt fitted by the authors (first order at 48.5 °C for P. luminescens luciferase; third order at 41 °C for P. leiognathi luciferase), hence evidence_level=inferred.

source_quote: Refolding kinetics analysis of other strains showed that thermal inactivated cells of B . subtilis wild-type strain 168 are substantially less capable of luciferase refolding than E . coli , and successfully refold just approximately one percent of available denatured enzymes.
notes: Cells were held at 51 °C until luminescence dropped to background (thermal inactivation took ~15-25 min), then translation was blocked with tetracycline and cultures were returned to room temperature; only ~1% of the denatured luciferase refolded (stated as 'approximately one percent'). Kinetic curves are in Figure 4.
